name: Paldra – AI Customer Service, Chatbot & Live Chat
author: Paldra

sections.description:
Paldra answers your visitors’ questions directly on your site, based on your own content. The chatbot reads your pages and answers from them. If something is not backed up by your content, it does not claim it: it says that it does not know yet and offers to pass the question on to your team.

This plugin connects your site to the Paldra service (https://paldra.com). A Paldra account is required; you can create one during the connection step and test it for 14 days without a payment method.

What makes Paldra different

  • Answers only from your own data: your public pages and, with WooCommerce, your products, prices, stock and shipping rules. No general internet knowledge mixed in.
  • Every statement is checked against its source before it is sent. What your content does not cover is removed, not guessed.
  • Hands over instead of guessing: if the answer is not in your content, the chatbot says so and passes the conversation to your team.
  • WooCommerce order status in the chat (only if you turn it on): status, tracking number and, for unpaid orders, WooCommerce’s own “Pay now” link. The plugin answers the lookup inside your store and only after the customer’s email address (or phone number) matches the order. No extra key to copy.
  • One inbox for website chat, email, WhatsApp and Instagram, so your team answers everything in one place.
  • Hosted in Germany (Hetzner), with a public data processing agreement.

What you get

  • AI chatbot that answers from your real page content
  • Live chat: take over any conversation yourself at any time
  • Shared team inbox for chat, email, WhatsApp and Instagram
  • No code: activate, approve, done. No theme edits, no snippet
  • Answers in the language of the question

All features run on the Paldra service. The plugin itself contains no locked features; it only connects your site and loads the chat widget.

Privacy

Operated and hosted in the EU (Germany). A data processing agreement (DPA) is available at https://paldra.com/avv

For order status questions (WooCommerce only, and only after you turned order status on), the order data your store returns after a successful match (status, date, item names and quantities, carrier, tracking number, payment link for unpaid orders) is processed by Paldra on your behalf to write the answer, and is stored as part of the conversation. Your store checks the customer’s email address or phone number itself; Paldra never receives addresses, names or prices from this endpoint. Details are listed under “External services” below.

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Paldra service (https://paldra.com), operated by Paldra, Germany. Without this connection the plugin has no function.

What is sent, and when:

  1. When you connect (once: right after you activate the plugin as an administrator, or when you click “Connect” under Settings -> Paldra): you are redirected to paldra.com. After you sign in, an approval page on paldra.com shows your site address and everything Paldra may do: show the chat widget on your site and, only if WooCommerce is active, read products, prices and stock (read only) and answer order status questions. Nothing is connected and nothing else is sent until you click “Connect” on that page; “Cancel” takes you back without connecting. The redirect sends your site address, a one-time callback token, the plugin version and, only if WooCommerce is active, the requested permission order_read. After you approve and return, the plugin exchanges a one-time code for a plugin token in a server-to-server request to https://paldra.com/api/integrations/wordpress/exchange (sent: the one-time code and your site address).
  2. WooCommerce (only if WooCommerce is active): after you approved the connection on the approval page, the plugin creates a WooCommerce REST API key with read-only permission in your own store and sends it, together with your shop ID and site address, to https://paldra.com/api/integrations/woocommerce/plugin/connect. Paldra uses it to read products, prices and stock so the chatbot can answer questions about them. “Disconnect” and uninstalling delete this key again.
  3. Catalog changes (only if WooCommerce is connected): when a product is created, updated, trashed or deleted, the plugin sends a short signal (shop ID, site address, the word “product”) to https://paldra.com/api/integrations/woocommerce/plugin/changed, at most once per minute. No product data is sent with it.
  4. Shipping email copy (only if you set it up in the Paldra dashboard): the plugin asks Paldra for your copy address at most every 12 hours (sent: shop ID, site address, the sender address of your WooCommerce emails) and adds it as BCC to the WooCommerce “Completed order” email. That copy contains what the email contains, for example the order number, the customer’s email address and the tracking number. Without this setup nothing is sent.
  5. Order status (only if WooCommerce is active, and only with your consent): the plugin registers its order status endpoint only after you agreed to it, either by clicking “Connect” on the approval page on paldra.com (which lists “Answer order status”) or by turning on “Order status in the chat” under Settings -> Paldra or in the admin notice. Updating the plugin never turns it on: after an update from 1.4.0 nothing new is sent automatically, a dismissible notice only offers the choice. When you agree, it registers its order status endpoint with Paldra at https://paldra.com/api/integrations/woocommerce/plugin/bestellabfrage (sent: shop ID, site address, the endpoint address and the read-only permission order_read) and receives a secret key that only your site and Paldra know. When a customer asks about an order in the chat or by email, Paldra calls the endpoint /wp-json/paldra/v1/order-status on your site with the order number and the email address (or phone number) the customer gave. The plugin checks them in your store. Only if they match the order does it return: order number, status, order date, item names and quantities, carrier and tracking number (if a tracking plugin stores them) and, only for orders that still need payment (pending or failed), WooCommerce’s “Pay now” link. It never returns addresses, names, prices or other customer data. If the details do not match, or the order does not exist, the answer is just “not found”. Every request is signed with the secret key (HMAC-SHA256), expires after 5 minutes and can be used only once; requests are rate-limited. Turning the switch off, “Disconnect” or deactivating the plugin unregisters the endpoint at Paldra.
  6. On your public pages: the chat widget script is loaded from https://paldra.com/public/widget.js with wp_enqueue_script. It is the only code the plugin loads from outside, and it runs in the visitor’s browser, not on your server. Loading it sends the usual browser request data (IP address, user agent, page URL) to paldra.com. Only when a visitor opens the chat and writes a message are the message and technical details (conversation ID, page URL, language) sent to Paldra to create the answer.

No chat content is sent while nobody uses the chat. The plugin never executes code received from the service; responses from Paldra are only read as data (tokens, status, copy address, secret key).

  • Service provider: Paldra – https://paldra.com
  • Terms of service: https://paldra.com/en/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://paldra.com/en/privacy
  • Data processing agreement: https://paldra.com/avv
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin from the WordPress plugin directory (or upload the ZIP under Plugins -> Add New -> Upload Plugin).
  2. Click Activate. You are taken straight to Paldra to connect your site – no settings page in between.
  3. Sign in to Paldra or create an account (14 days free, no payment method).
  4. Paldra shows one approval page with everything it may do on your site. Click Connect.
  5. You are brought back to WordPress automatically and the chat widget is live. If WooCommerce is installed, it is connected at the same time, including order status in the chat.

If you activated several plugins at once, or via WP-CLI, open Settings -> Paldra and click Connect.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Paldra account?

Yes. You can create one when you connect and test it for 14 days without a payment method.

Do I have to change my theme?

No. The plugin loads the widget itself through wp_enqueue_script. No snippet, no child theme, no code.

How does the chatbot know what is on my site?

Paldra reads your public pages and builds a knowledge base from them. You can view, extend and refresh it in the Paldra dashboard at any time.

What happens when it does not know something?

It says so and offers to pass the question on to your team. It does not make up an answer.

Can I take over a conversation?

Yes. In the Paldra inbox you see running conversations and can answer yourself at any time; the bot then steps back.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. When WooCommerce is active, the approval page on Paldra lists what is connected: products, prices and stock through a read-only key, and order status through the plugin’s own signed endpoint. You can turn order status on or off at any time under Settings -> Paldra. Customers get status, tracking number and, for unpaid orders, the “Pay now” link, only after their email address (or phone number) matches the order.

I updated from 1.4.0. Is order status turned on automatically?

No. Updating sends nothing new. A dismissible notice in the admin area offers “Turn on” or “Not now”, and the switch “Order status in the chat” under Settings -> Paldra stays available.

Do I still need the “WooCommerce (orders)” card with my own REST key in Paldra?

No, not with version 2.0.0 or later once order status is turned on. An existing card keeps working as a fallback.

Where do tracking numbers come from?

WooCommerce itself has no tracking numbers. The plugin reads them from WooCommerce Shipment Tracking or Advanced Shipment Tracking (field _wc_shipment_tracking_items). Other sources can add them with the filter paldra_order_shipments. Shops with their own order numbers can map them with the filter paldra_order_id_for_number.

Can I hide the widget on certain pages?

Yes, with the filter paldra_widget_enabled, for example:
add_filter( ‘paldra_widget_enabled’, function ( $on ) { return is_page( ‘imprint’ ) ? false : $on; } );

How do I remove the widget?

Deactivate the plugin. Nothing is loaded anymore. Uninstalling also removes all plugin settings, the WooCommerce key the plugin created and the plugin’s table of one-time values.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

  • Approval page: connecting now ends on one page on paldra.com that shows your site address and everything Paldra may do (chat widget; with WooCommerce: read products, prices and stock, answer order status). Nothing is connected until you click “Connect” there; “Cancel” takes you back without connecting.
  • One-click setup: right after you activate the plugin, WordPress takes you straight to that approval page – no detour via an empty settings page. This happens once, only for administrators, only when activating this single plugin, and not via WP-CLI, AJAX or network activation.
  • New settings page under Settings -> Paldra: a clear “Connect” card when not connected; when connected, the live status (chat, WooCommerce), a switch “Order status in the chat”, shortcuts to Paldra and to your site, and a small chat preview.
  • WooCommerce order status without a second key, only with your consent: Paldra asks the plugin, and the plugin checks order number plus email address (or phone number) inside your store. Only on a match does it return status, date, items (name and quantity), carrier and tracking number, and for unpaid orders (pending or failed) WooCommerce’s “Pay now” link. Wrong details and unknown numbers both return “not found”.
  • Security: every order status request is signed (HMAC-SHA256 with a secret only your site and Paldra know, bound to method and endpoint), expires after 5 minutes, works only once (one-time values are kept in a small table of their own, {prefix}paldra_nonces, for 10 minutes) and is rate-limited (per site and per order number).
  • Compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS): orders are only read through WooCommerce’s own order functions.
  • Updating from 1.4.0 turns nothing on and sends nothing new. A dismissible notice offers “Turn on” or “Not now”; the switch on the settings page stays available.
  • The “not connected yet” notice can now be dismissed.
  • Turning the switch off, “Disconnect” and deactivating the plugin unregister the order status endpoint at Paldra; uninstalling removes the secret key and the table of one-time values.
  • Unchanged: the connection security (one-time token, confirmation for connections not started from WordPress) and the WooCommerce catalog connection.

1.4.0

  • Shipping email copy: if you set up “Shipping email copy” in the Paldra dashboard, the WooCommerce “Completed order” email gets your copy address as BCC, so the chat can tell customers where their parcel is. Without that setup nothing happens.
  • English is now the source language of the plugin; a German translation is included.
  • Uninstalling now also removes the plugin token, the WooCommerce settings and the read-only WooCommerce key.

1.3.0

  • WooCommerce is connected automatically when you connect: the plugin creates a key with read-only permission in your own store. No extra step.
  • Catalog changes (product created, updated, deleted) are reported automatically, at most once per minute.
  • “Disconnect” removes the created key from WooCommerce again.

1.2.0

  • After activation the plugin takes you straight to the connection page.
  • As long as the site is not connected, a notice in the admin area shows the way there.

1.1.0

  • Security: a callback without a valid one-time token no longer connects the site silently; it now requires explicit confirmation in the admin area.
  • Security: the Paldra address is only accepted with https, also when reading a stored value.
  • New: “Disconnect” in the admin area.
  • New: uninstalling removes options and transients (uninstall.php).
  • New: filter paldra_widget_enabled to hide the widget on single pages.
  • New: “Settings” link in the plugin list.
  • The widget is now loaded through wp_enqueue_script.

1.0.0

  • First version for the WordPress plugin directory.
